Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Scanner / Reconnaissance Burst Against Banking Applications - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source generated a burst (>=100 in 30 min) of reconnaissance-class WAF violations - Vulnerability Scan, Forceful Browsing, Predictable Resource Location, Non-browser Client, Information Leakage. Triage question: is this hostile pre-attack mapping of the banking apps, or an approved scanner / benign crawler?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Recon precedes exploitation; identifying and blocking the scanner early denies the attacker their target map. Distinguishing hostile from approved scanners avoids wasted effort.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps
Published banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog -> logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor F5)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields: deviceCustomString4=attack_type, deviceCustomNumber2=violation_rating (>=4 = real attack), deviceCustomString1=security policy, requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceCustomNumber1=HTTP response code, deviceCustomString6=source geo, cef.name=violation name, event.action=passed|alerted|blocked.

Signal.Name: Recon burst
Signal.Details: >=100 recon-class violations from one source in 30 min.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Approved internal scanners (Nessus-class) and search-engine crawlers are the main benign causes; an external source doing forceful-browsing + info-leakage then shifting to exploit types is hostile.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the recon source is an approved/benign scanner or a hostile actor mapping the estate, and whether it escalated to exploitation.

Step.name: Recon type and target breakdown
Step.Purpose: Characterise the recon: which violation types, which apps/URLs, how broad.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), apps = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1), urls = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.requestUrl), geo = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), ua_class = VALUES(cef.name) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: High distinct-URL count = directory/resource enumeration. Non-browser Client + Vulnerability Scan types together = an automated scanner. Foreign geo raises hostility.

Step.name: Did the recon escalate to actual exploitation
Step.Purpose: A source that reconnoiters then sends rating>=4 exploit types is the dangerous case - recon is just the prelude.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 IN ("SQL-Injection","Cross Site Scripting (XSS)","Command Execution","Remote File Include","Server Side Code Injection","Path Traversal") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS exploit_events = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4), passed = COUNT(CASE(event.action == "passed", 1, null)) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Any exploit-class events from the same source turn this from recon into an active attack - escalate and pivot to PB-F5-001/004. Empty = recon only (still worth blocking if hostile).

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the source escalated to exploit-class attacks (esp. any passed).
Node.Result: True Positive (Recon Escalated to Exploitation - escalate, block, review targets)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows broad hostile enumeration (many URLs, forceful browsing, info leakage) from an external/foreign source with no benign identity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Hostile Reconnaissance - block source, monitor for return)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the source is a documented internal scanner (e.g. Nessus) or a known search-engine crawler.
External automated source, unclear intent, no escalation yet.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-F5SCAN-PROFILE, INV-02-F5SCAN-ESCALATION to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An approved scanner or a legitimate search-engine/monitoring crawler.

Indicators.Item: Internal known scanner IP or verified crawler (reverse-DNS/UA).

SOCAction.Item: Allowlist verified crawlers / exception the scanner source.

TruePositive.Definition: Hostile reconnaissance mapping the banking apps for later attack.

Indicators.Item: Broad URL/resource enumeration from an external source.

SOCAction.Item: Block the source; watch for its return from new IPs.
If escalated: treat as active attack and review targeted resources.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured internal tool or health-check hammering the apps and tripping recon signatures.

Indicators.Item: Repetitive requests to a fixed URL set flagged as forceful browsing.

SOCAction.Item: Tune the health-check or the policy; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the source; block if hostile external.
If escalated to exploitation: pivot to the exploitation playbooks.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Monitor for the source returning via new IPs; review resources it enumerated.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Deploy bot defense / rate-limiting on public apps; allowlist verified crawlers.

QualityChecks.Check: Recon type list matches the scanner rule; threshold 100/30m from the measured baseline.
Non-browser Client + Vulnerability Scan are strong automation signals.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Source blocked; no escalation; enumerated resources reviewed.
